This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   Build a complete invoicing system incrementally over 18 requests. The user established core "house rules" at the outset: money as integer cents (using roundCents()), never throw on bad input (return fail(CODE) instead), never mutate arguments, and always run npm test before declaring completion. Each request adds a specific feature, building on prior work. The most recent request (18th) asks to add lateFee(invoice, asOf) to src/reports.js, calculating 0.04% of amount due per day the invoice is overdue, or 0 if not overdue.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Result pattern: ok(value) or fail(error) from result.js
   - Monetary calculation: all amounts in integer cents using roundCents()
   - Invoice workflow: draft → issued → partially_paid/paid
   - Line calculations: qty × unitPrice, then discount applied, then VAT on remainder
   - Customer tiers: gold (5%), silver (2.5%), standard (0%) automatic discounts
   - Date handling: UTC-based, YYYY-MM-DD strings, daysBetween() for calculations
   - Invoice numbering: INV-YYYY-NNNN with separate counter per year
   - Credit note numbering: CN-YYYY-NNNN with separate counter per year
   - Payment terms: NET14, NET30 (default), EOM with automatic due date calculation
   - VAT rates: per-line (21%, 9%, 0%), calculated on post-discount amount
   - Vouchers: fixed-amount deductions applied after VAT
   - Reporting: statements, overdue tracking, VAT summary

3. Files and Code Sections:

   src/errors.js:
   - Added error codes throughout development: CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND, DATE_INVALID, DISCOUNT_INVALID, LINE_NOT_FOUND, NO_LINES, NOT_DRAFT, NOT_ISSUED, OVERPAYMENT, QTY_INVALID, TERMS_INVALID, UNKNOWN_SKU, VOUCHER_EXISTS, CREDIT_TOO_HIGH, AMOUNT_INVALID, CUSTOMER_INVALID

   src/invoices.js:
   - createInvoice({ customerId, issueDate, lines, terms }): Creates draft invoice with validation, applies tier discounts automatically to lines, validates date format/calendar validity, validates quantities, validates SKUs, calculates due dates based on terms
   - addLine(invoice, { sku, qty, discountPercent }): Adds line to draft invoice or increases qty if SKU exists
   - removeLine(invoice, sku): Removes line from draft, prevents last line removal
   - issueInvoice(invoice, existingNumbers): Generates invoice number and changes status to issued
   - applyVoucher(invoice, { code, amount }): Applies fixed voucher discount to draft invoice only
   - lineTotal(line): Returns qty × unitPrice
   - lineDiscount(line): Returns discountPercent-based discount rounded
   - lineVat(line): Returns VAT on line amount after discount
   - invoiceTotals(invoice): Returns { subtotal, discount, vat, voucher, total } with total = subtotal - discount + vat - voucher, clamped at 0

   src/customers.js:
   - normalizeId(id): Trims whitespace and converts to uppercase
   - getCustomer(id): Fetches customer after normalizing ID
   - TIER_DISCOUNTS constant: { gold: 5, silver: 2.5, standard: 0 }

   src/dates.js:
   - isValidDate(text): Validates YYYY-MM-DD format and real calendar date using UTC
   - addDays(date, n): Adds days to date in UTC, returns YYYY-MM-DD
   - daysBetween(a, b): Returns whole days from a to b using UTC

   src/numbering.js:
   - nextInvoiceNumber(existingNumbers, issueDate): Generates INV-YYYY-NNNN with separate counter per year

   src/payments.js:
   - recordPayment(invoice, { amount, date }): Records payment on issued/partially_paid invoice, updates status to paid when balance reaches 0
   - balanceDue(invoice): Returns total - sum of payments

   src/render.js:
   - renderInvoiceText(invoice): Renders plain-text invoice for customer display, shows DRAFT or invoice number, customer name, line details with discounts, subtotal/discount/VAT/total lines

   src/credits.js:
   - nextCreditNoteNumber(existingNumbers, date): Generates CN-YYYY-NNNN with separate counter per year
   - createCreditNote(invoice, { amount, reason, date }, existingNumbers): Creates credit note for issued/partially_paid/paid invoices, validates amount doesn't exceed invoice total

   src/statements.js:
   - statement(customerId, invoices, asOf): Returns customer statement with invoices due, filters by customerId/status/date, calculates totalDue

   src/reports.js:
   - overdueInvoices(invoices, asOf): Returns overdue invoices sorted by daysOverdue descending, includes number/customerId/dueDate/daysOverdue/due
   - vatSummary(invoices): Returns VAT grouped by rate { rate, base, vat } sorted by rate descending, base calculated after discounts

   test/invoices.test.js, test/customers.test.js, test/dates.test.js, test/numbering.test.js, test/payments.test.js, test/render.test.js, test/credits.test.js, test/statements.test.js, test/reports.test.js:
   - Comprehensive test coverage for all features, currently 253 tests passing

4. Errors and fixes:
   - Test calculation error in VAT summary tests: Expected base and VAT amounts not accounting for tier discounts. Fixed by calculating base = lineTotal - lineDiscount for each test.
   - Multiple tests for overdueInvoices, invoiceTotals, and other calculations initially had incorrect expected values when tier discounts were automatically applied. These were systematically found through test failures and corrected by accounting for the 5% gold tier discount and 2.5% silver tier discount in test expectations.

5. Problem Solving:
   The main challenge was ensuring monetary calculations remained accurate through multiple discount layers (tier discount + line discount + VAT). This was solved by establishing the calculation order: line total → apply line discount → apply VAT to remainder → apply voucher. All calculations use roundCents() to handle fractional cents. The tests validated this order worked correctly across different VAT rates (21%, 9%, 0%).

Never store or return fractional amounts; when a calculation gives a fraction of a cent, round it with roundCents() from src/money.js. 2. Never throw for bad input. Return fail(CODE) from src/result.js, and add every new error code to ERRORS in src/errors.js with a one-line message. 3. Never mutate an argument. Return new objects and arrays instead. 4. Run `npm test` before you say a request is done. [First request: createInvoice]"

7. Pending Tasks:
   - Add lateFee(invoice, asOf) function to src/reports.js
   - Function should calculate: 0.04% × amount due × days overdue (or 0 if not overdue)
   - Add comprehensive tests for lateFee function
   - Run npm test to verify all 253+ tests pass

8. Current Work:
   The user has just provided the 18th request to add late fees functionality. The request asks for lateFee(invoice, asOf) to be added to src/reports.js with calculation: 0.04% of amount still due per day overdue. The function should return 0 if the invoice is not overdue. This builds on the existing reports.js which already contains overdueInvoices(invoices, asOf) and vatSummary(invoices) functions. The user has also requested lateFee tests be added. Current test status: 253 passing tests.

9. Optional Next Step:
   The user's most recent explicit request is: "Late fees. Add lateFee(invoice, asOf) to src/reports.js: 0.04% of the amount still due for every day the invoice is overdue (days from its dueDate to asOf), and 0 if it isn't overdue. Add tests." This requires implementing a lateFee function that calculates the late fee based on: (1) using balanceDue(invoice) to get amount due, (2) using daysBetween(invoice.dueDate, asOf) to get days overdue, (3) returning 0 if days overdue is negative, (4) otherwise returning roundCents(amountDue × 0.0004 × daysOverdue). Tests should verify: single overdue invoice, multiple days, not-yet-due invoices return 0, due-on-date returns 0, multiple invoices, and calculation accuracy.
